items.item: A run event's additive design (later events for the same run only add detail, never replace a prior one) is what lets a long-running job emit a START immediately and fill in its outputs only once it actually knows them at COMPLETE — the model fits streaming emission, not just a single final report.

items.item: A facet's own versioned _schemaURL is what makes the format extensible without breaking old consumers: a consumer that has never heard of a given facet name can skip it entirely and still correctly read every facet it does recognise.

at.step: Reveal: facets, attached and versioned

items.item: Naming the Airflow provider's legacy predecessor as unmaintained, with a version cutoff, is the same kind of fact this chapter flagged for Amundsen in the catalog topic — a status a syllabus can freeze that a primary source keeps moving past.

That Marquez, DataHub and a cloud catalog can all consume the same OpenLineage event stream is the direct payoff of the catalog topic's own architecture point: a graph of entities and named edges is exactly the shape an inbound lineage event fills in, whichever catalog is doing the filling.

OpenTelemetry and OpenLineage sharing only the idea of a run identifier, not the rest of their data, is why a trace and a lineage graph have to be joined deliberately rather than merged automatically — this topic is the lineage half of that pair the tracing topic named but didn't build.

at.quote: OTel (operational telemetry) vs OpenLineage (lineage metadata) as complements

items.item: The parent run facet's own worked example (an Airflow DAG execution spawning tasks which spawn Spark jobs) is the same three-hop chain this topic's own lab reproduces in miniature — a task's run naming the DAG run that triggered it.

items.item: SQL-text parsing and runtime-plan traversal disagreeing on the exact same query is not a bug in one of them — they are answering different questions (what the query says versus what the engine resolved it to), and a design that only has the text-parsed graph has quietly accepted the smaller answer.

items.item: The predict question's two scenarios (a CASE and a parameterised table name, then a daily job's date-built table name) both test the same underlying claim from different angles: lineage collection records exactly what it was shown, nothing it could reasonably infer about what a human would call the same dataset.

at.step: Prove it

items.item: A column-lineage comparison that shows the runtime path finding strictly more edges than the text-parsed path, never fewer, is the honest shape of the claim — text parsing is a subset of what plan traversal sees, not a different and sometimes-better alternative to it.

at.step: Reveal: reading text versus reading the plan

items.item: This topic's lab posts real, schema-shaped events to a local HTTP receiver at Marquez's own ingestion path rather than to Marquez itself — a deliberate, disclosed scope limit (no Docker or JVM catalog on the build machine), not a claim that the full reference server was exercised.
